title: Fixed-order or unique invariant random-order dichotomy for transitive countably infinite categorical structures without algebraicity and with weak elimination of imaginaries
source_title: Invariant measures on products and on the space of linear orders
author: Colin Jahel; Todor Tsankov
difficulty_reason: The cited unitary representation results do not classify invariant random orders on the smaller automorphism group. The authors obtain the required conditional independence, reconstruct uniform orders from non-atomic conditional statistics, and use alternating type paths together with successive atomic conditioning to force a Dirac invariant order in the remaining case. Those compatibility and conditioning constructions give the dichotomy before the final ergodic-decomposition step.

proof_review.note: Full article retained as conservative closed context for notation, global assumptions, diagrams and references. Exact primary and supporting physical proof pages are recorded separately. Exact Theorem4.1, equivalently1.2, for countably infinite transitive aleph0-categorical structures with no algebraicity and weak elimination of imaginaries. Dichotomy between an Aut(M)-fixed linear order and the uniform measure as the unique invariant Borel probability measure on all LO(M). Complete new imaginary-closure and Hilbert-support independence proof9–12, order reconstruction, disjoint alternating paths, atomic conditioning and final finite-type induction14–19 read. Tsankov2012 oligomorphic representation classification is an explicit previously established research foundation, as are standard conditional-expectation/independence and ergodic decomposition. The type-path construction concerns types of distinct elements, not the equality type, as its definition and all pairwise-distinct uses explicitly require; this harmless diagonal bookkeeping does not add a construction. Final induction index after its last type is unused. No arbitrary nontransitive structures, proper subflow classification or amenability/ordering-property corollary counted separately.
